turns.t: Hi, hi. I'm worried about my hands, they're awful, they're cracked and bleeding, and I'm scared it's going to get infected. I work in a care home, and we wash our hands constantly.
That sounds sore. When did it start?
Oh, a few months, I think, or since the winter, I can't remember when it began, maybe before. I keep meaning to come.
Which parts of the hands?
Between the fingers, and the backs, and my knuckles are split. And the skin's red, and itchy.
Any weeping or crusting, any yellow, any signs of infection?
A bit of crusting on one knuckle. No pus.
Do you wear gloves at work? ~
When I'm told to, but they make my hands sweat, and then it's worse. ~
What have you tried? ~
A hand cream from the supermarket, I use it when I remember. Which is not often, to be fair. ~
Is there any eczema in the past, or asthma, hay fever?
I had eczema as a child.
How many times a day do you wash your hands?
Thirty, forty times a shift. And sanitiser, the gel, it stings.
Do you have any other work involving chemicals, like cleaning products?
Yes, the cleaning products, bleach and disinfectant.
Pulse and temperature first, please. ~
Okay. ~
Pulse 78, temperature 36.7.
Good. ~
Now let me see the hands.
They're embarrassing. ~
There are dry, red, scaly patches with deep cracks across the knuckles, and in the finger webs, and one knuckle has a crust, but there's no spreading redness or pus.
Is it eczema, then? ~
It looks like irritant contact dermatitis, caused by the constant washing and cleaning products.
Can it be cured? ~
It can be controlled. I'm going to start you on a steroid ointment, betamethasone, apply it once a day to the red areas, for two weeks, and a thick emollient.
Do I have to use them all the time? ~
Steroid once a day, thin layer, only on the red cracked areas, and the emollient, as often as you can, particularly after washing.
Okay. I'll try, I promise. ~
Wear cotton gloves under waterproof ones, use a soap substitute, and dry your hands carefully.
I'll try. Sorry. ~
And I'd like to take a swab from the crusted knuckle, and a skin patch test referral, because I'd like to rule out a reaction to something at work.
Okay. ~
Please let your manager know, occupational health may help with a different glove.
Good idea. ~
